notice: Indicative estimates only - NOT predictions for this patient. Recovery depends on the cause, severity, other illnesses and how quickly treatment starts; costs vary widely by city, hospital and plan. Written for the SwasthyaSetu demo from general clinical knowledge; to be reviewed by a clinician before real use.
government_note: At government PHC/CHC/district hospitals, consultation, many tests and essential medicines are free under the National Free Drugs and Free Diagnostics Service Initiatives. Hospital admission can be covered under Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY for eligible families.

Hyperglycemia.recovery: Long-term condition - managed, not cured. Sugar control usually improves within 4-12 weeks of treatment; HbA1c reflects the last ~3 months.
Hyperglycemia.cost_private: Rs 1,500-5,000 for the first visit and tests; Rs 300-2,000 a month for medicines

Impaired glucose regulation.recovery: Often reversible with diet, exercise and weight loss over 3-6 months.
Impaired glucose regulation.cost_private: Rs 800-2,500 for review and repeat tests

Dyslipidemia / elevated cardiovascular r.recovery: Cholesterol improves 6-12 weeks after diet change or medicine; treatment is usually long-term.
Dyslipidemia / elevated cardiovascular r.cost_private: Rs 1,000-3,000 for review and tests; Rs 200-1,000 a month for medicines

Iron-deficiency anemia pattern.recovery: Haemoglobin usually starts rising within 2-4 weeks of iron; body stores take about 3 months. The cause of blood loss must also be found.
Iron-deficiency anemia pattern.cost_private: Rs 500-3,000 (more if iron injections or transfusion are needed)

Liver enzyme elevation / hepatitis patte.recovery: Depends on the cause - from a few weeks (viral, medicine-related) to long-term (fatty liver, alcohol). Needs evaluation first.

Viral hepatitis.recovery: Hepatitis A/E usually settle in 4-8 weeks; hepatitis B can be long-term and needs specialist follow-up.
Viral hepatitis.cost_private: Rs 2,000-10,000 for evaluation; testing and treatment are free under the National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme

Renal impairment.recovery: Sudden (acute) kidney injury may recover over days to weeks; chronic kidney disease is long-term and needs regular monitoring.
Renal impairment.cost_private: Rs 2,000-10,000 for evaluation; dialysis costs much more (covered under PM-JAY for eligible families)

Urinary tract infection pattern.recovery: Usually better within 3-7 days of the right treatment.

Systemic inflammation with autoimmune ma.recovery: Usually long-term; symptoms are brought under control over weeks to months with specialist care.

Hypothyroid-pattern thyroid dysfunction.recovery: TSH usually normalises 6-8 weeks after starting tablets; treatment is often lifelong.
Hypothyroid-pattern thyroid dysfunction.cost_private: Rs 500-1,500 for review and tests; Rs 100-300 a month for medicine

Hyperthyroid-pattern thyroid dysfunction.recovery: Symptoms usually controlled in 1-3 months; treatment often continues 12-18 months.

Thyroid in pregnancy.recovery: Monitored and adjusted throughout pregnancy and after delivery.
Thyroid in pregnancy.cost_private: Rs 500-2,000 per review; antenatal care is free at government facilities

Vitamin D deficiency.recovery: Levels usually correct in 8-12 weeks of supplements.

Vitamin B12 deficiency.recovery: Blood counts improve within weeks; nerve symptoms can take months.

Elevated CA-125.recovery: A raised CA-125 is not a diagnosis - it has many causes. Needs specialist evaluation before any time frame can be given.

Elevated PSA.recovery: A raised PSA is not a diagnosis - infection or enlargement can also raise it. Needs specialist evaluation first.

Multi-system screening abnormalities.recovery: Depends on which findings are confirmed on review.
Multi-system screening abnormalities.cost_private: Rs 1,000-5,000 for review and repeat tests

2D Echo.recovery: Depends on the heart finding - from routine follow-up to long-term treatment.

Malaria.recovery: Usually recovers in 1-2 weeks with prompt treatment; severe malaria needs hospital admission.
Malaria.cost_private: Rs 1,000-5,000 (Rs 10,000+ if admitted); testing and treatment are free at government facilities

Typhoid.recovery: Fever usually settles 3-5 days into the right antibiotics; full recovery takes 2-4 weeks.

Dengue.recovery: Usually 1-2 weeks. Days 3-7 are the riskiest - watch for warning signs (bleeding, severe stomach pain, vomiting, drowsiness).

Ultrasound abdomen.recovery: Depends on what the ultrasound shows - a doctor needs to review it.
Ultrasound abdomen.cost_private: Rs 1,000-5,000 for review and follow-up tests

Chest X-ray.recovery: Depends on the finding - e.g. pneumonia usually improves in 1-3 weeks; other findings need further tests.

CT.recovery: Depends on what the CT shows - needs specialist review.
CT.cost_private: Rs 2,000-15,000 for specialist review and next steps

MRI brain.recovery: Depends on the finding - needs a neurologist's review before any time frame.

TMT.recovery: Depends on the result - from reassurance to further heart tests.

ECG.recovery: Some ECG changes need same-day evaluation; outcome depends on the cause.

PCOS-pattern.recovery: Long-term management; cycles often become more regular over 3-6 months with treatment and lifestyle change.

Pregnancy.recovery: Antenatal care continues through pregnancy (at least four check-ups).
Pregnancy.cost_private: Rs 0 at government facilities (free antenatal care and delivery under JSSK); private antenatal care costs vary widely
